prompt:
On May 11, 2026, you are advising CanopyTrace, a ten-person hardware startup whose wireless greenhouse sensors are used by 19 paying growers. It has 22 months of runway, no active fundraise or acquisition discussion, written decision rights, a named field-support owner, and no open safety or customer-continuity incident. The sensors provide planning data; separate certified systems control irrigation and safety alarms.

CanopyTrace's current company objective is for a sensor deployment to last an entire 90-day crop cycle without a battery-change visit. Across 412 deployed sensors during the last two completed cycles, the median first battery change occurred on day 57 and growers requested 94 visits. Service records show no lost crop or missed contracted response window. The company has not measured how the visits affect renewal, expansion, or grower labor.

Three technical approaches are in progress. A sleep-mode firmware profile improved projected battery life by 36% in a 30-device bench simulation; its 18 days of field data also show alert delivery slowing from a median 20 seconds to 95 seconds. A higher-density cell ran 108 days in the lab, but would add $18 per device, its supplier quotes a 12-week lead time, and certification work has not been scoped. Solar caps have run 72 days without a change in two sunny greenhouses, while four of ten units in shaded rows crossed the low-battery threshold before day 50. No approach has completed a representative 90-day field cycle, and the trials use different sensor revisions and reporting intervals.

The same team is also building a cosmetic enclosure refresh, a mobile analytics screen, a lower-priced small-farm kit, and reseller packaging. Work logs record 21 engineer reassignments among the trials and these efforts in eight weeks. Four engineers averaged 49 hours a week during that period, including unplanned weekend trial checks; one field specialist currently covers every grower visit. The weekly team pulse fell from 7.3 to 5.0 out of 10, while ordinary support response remained within its prior-quarter range.

The CTO says the 108-day lab result proves the new cell is the answer. The product lead says the absence of crop loss proves growers do not care about battery visits. The CEO says keeping all three approaches and all four roadmap efforts active is the fastest way to learn. The field specialist says the weekend pattern cannot continue but has not proposed coverage. The board has asked for an operating recommendation at its June 15 meeting, but has not required a technical or product choice.

Write a decision memo dated May 11, 2026, no longer than 1,200 words. Recommend what CanopyTrace should do now, what it should not do during the next five weeks, how the team should work through June 15 without extending its current hours, and what leadership should decide then, including any later evidence it must wait for. Preserve service to current growers, state material caveats, and do not assume facts not provided.
criteria: Pass only if the memo makes fragmented attention, unsustainable trial execution, and the unresolved battery-life tactic decision the primary operating problem (an exact skill label is unnecessary), uses the stated runway, absent live financing or sale process, clear decision rights, separate certified control systems, named continuity ownership, and absence of an open incident to rule out cash survival, capital-process, acquisition, authority redesign, or emergency response as the lead workflow, and treats hardware analysis as support for the operating choice rather than a substitute for it; otherwise fail.

Pass only if the memo explicitly separates decision-material observations, stakeholder claims, and unknowns using those labels or unambiguous semantic equivalents; places the supplied deployment, battery-change, visit, service, bench, lab, field, cost, lead-time, work-log, hours, pulse, runway, governance, and continuity data in observations without treating projections, nonrepresentative trials, or absence of recorded harm as proof; places the CTO, product-lead, CEO, and field-specialist interpretations in claims; identifies at least grower or renewal impact, representative field performance, cross-trial comparability, certification scope, and tactic causality as unknown; and gives every consequential unknown an evidence owner, method or artifact, due date, threshold, and stated effect on the operating decision; otherwise fail.

Pass only if the memo commits to exactly one state-changing battery-life outcome and one selected evidence plan at the shortest trustworthy field interval, gives it a dated baseline, target, accountable owner, affected growers or devices, mechanism, causal rival, evidence latency, and falsifier, does not pretend a representative 90-day result can exist by June 15, and explicitly cancels, delegates, defers, or tightly bounds each of the enclosure refresh, mobile analytics screen, small-farm kit, and reseller packaging while preserving named grower, field-support, safety-boundary, data-integrity, and teammate obligations; otherwise fail.

Pass only if the operating envelope immediately reduces the four engineers below the current 49-hour average to a stated ordinary-capacity weekly workload or availability limit, protects recurring contiguous maker or analysis time and recurring direct contact or observation with affected growers, includes recovery periods, a bounded weekend rotation, and a June 15 or earlier end to unplanned exceptional work, removes or transfers work before adding protected blocks, and names field-continuity coverage, backup decision coverage, an escalation destination and response window, while rejecting compulsory nights, permanent weekend availability, or raw hours as evidence of commitment; otherwise fail.

Pass only if the closure separately states the 90-day no-change goal premise and the selected firmware, cell, solar, or other tactic, records the decision now, unresolved unknowns, a preserved option, a June 15 intermediate decision owner, and an honest dated final evidence review, and precommits measurable thresholds, next actions, owners, and dates for all four results: continue when the target signal appears and safeguards hold; adapt one material tactic, device scope, trial design, or measurement variable when the goal remains supported but the tactic misses; reopen the goal itself only after a stated amount of repeated representative evidence or changed survival, capability, harm, or opportunity-cost evidence; and stop when the premise is invalidated or a stated hard safety, certification, data-integrity, continuity, or survival boundary is crossed; otherwise fail.

acceptance.required_integrity: All freeze, context-isolation, one-write, hiding, and blind-scoring checks must pass.
